facts.statement: The genus Rolfosteus was described by Dennis and Miles in 1979.
Rolfosteus lived during the Early Frasnian stage of the Late Devonian period and was found in the Gogo Formation of Western Australia.
facts.quote: Rolfosteus is an extinct monospecific genus of arthrodire placoderm from the Early Frasnian stage of the Late Devonian period, found at the Gogo Formation of Western Australia.

facts.statement: Rolfosteus possessed sharp, bony plates on its mouth that formed a turtle-like beak used for cutting prey.
facts.quote: Like other arthrodires, such as Coccosteus and the giant Dunkleosteus, it had sharp, bony plates on its mouth which formed a turtle-like beak for cutting prey to pieces.

facts.statement: Rolfosteus had a highly elongated snout that researchers suggest may have enhanced its sense of smell and improved streamlining for hunting as a pelagic predator.
facts.quote: Rolfosteus's most unusual feature was its highly elongated rostrum (snout), which may have been used to enhance its sense of smell as well as increase its hydrodynamic streamlining, making it well adapted to be a pelagic pursuit predator.

facts.statement: Rolfosteus had fast jaw movement and specific jaw morphology that allowed it to capture and swallow prey whole.
facts.quote: Its fast jaw movement and jaw morphology allowed it to effectively capture prey and swallow them whole.

facts.statement: Rolfosteus is classified within the family Camuropiscidae, superfamily Incisoscutoidea, and the clade Coccosteomorphi.
facts.quote: Phylogeny Rolfosteus is a member of the family Camuropiscidae under the superfamily Incisoscutoidea, which belongs to the clade Coccosteomorphi, one of the two major clades within Eubrachythoraci.

facts.statement: Rolfosteus lived between 382.31 and 379 million years ago during the Frasnian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Frasnian to Frasnian (382.31 to 379 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Rolfosteus had a skull measuring 11.5 cm and tough plating on the front of its body.
rejected.quote: Rolfosteus had a skull reaching 11.5 cm, with tough plating on the front of its body.
